origin.description: Profile empirical log likelihood for a mean.
origin.usage:
EL.profile(y, tmin = min(y) + 0.1, tmax = max(y) - 0.1, n.t = 25,
          u = function(y, t) y - t)

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: A vector or matrix of data.

arguments.name: tmin
arguments.text: Smallest parameter on the grid. It must be larger than min(y).

arguments.name: tmax
arguments.text: Largest parameter on the grid. It must be smaller than max(y).

arguments.name: n.t
arguments.text: Number of parameter values between tmin and tmax.

arguments.name: u
arguments.text: Function of the data and the parameter. The default is y - t.

origin.details: The profile is for the practicals in chapter 10 of Davison and Hinkley (1997). At each grid point the source maximises the empirical log likelihood with nlm, then stores nlm's $x. nlm returns estimate, and a logical NA from the objective aborts the optimizer, so the installed function stops on R 4.5.
origin.value: A matrix with n.t rows. Column 1 is the parameter, column 2 is the centered empirical log likelihood, and column 3 is the Lagrange multiplier.

translation.description: Profile empirical log likelihood for a mean.

arguments.name: tmin
arguments.text: Smallest parameter on the grid. None uses min(y) + 0.1.

arguments.name: tmax
arguments.text: Largest parameter on the grid. None uses max(y) - 0.1.

arguments.name: n_t
arguments.text: Number of parameter values between tmin and tmax.

arguments.name: u
arguments.text: Function of the data and the parameter. None uses y - t.

translation.details: The grid and the centered log likelihood follow the source. The objective returns a numeric missing value when a trial step leaves the constraint, and the stored multiplier is nlm's estimate. A start whose code is above 2 is divided by 5 and tried again, up to 20 times.
translation.value: An n_t by 3 array. Column 1 is the parameter, column 2 is the centered empirical log likelihood, and column 3 is the Lagrange multiplier.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from boot.profile import el_profile

y = np.array([76, 79, 81, 79, 77, 79, 79, 78, 79, 82, 76, 73, 64], dtype=float)
print(el_profile(y, tmin=75, tmax=80, n_t=5))
